prompt.en: Two plants make the same number of new cells each day. In plant X, some new cells stay meristematic, and many others become permanent tissues for support and transport. In plant Y, almost all the new cells keep dividing. Which plant is more likely to grow into a tall, working plant? Give reasons.

label.en: Plant X is more likely to grow tall and work

level1.en: Which plant ends up with cells that can hold it up and carry water?

clue.en: Support and transport come from permanent tissues, and only plant X makes many of them.

level2Template.en: Plant ___ is more likely to grow into a tall, working plant.

label.en: Permanent tissues form when new cells differentiate

level1.en: What must happen to new cells before they can give support or carry water?

clue.en: New cells must stop dividing and change in structure and function. This process has a name.

level2Template.en: New cells must undergo ___ to become supporting and transport tissues.

label.en: Plant Y stays a mass of similar dividing cells

level1.en: What would plant Y be made of if almost all its cells kept dividing?

clue.en: Cells that keep dividing stay small and alike, so plant Y would have no strong support and no transport tubes.

level2Template.en: Plant Y would stay a soft mass of ___ cells, with no support or transport.

text.en: Plant X is more likely to grow into a tall, working plant.
In plant X, many new cells differentiate: they stop dividing and become permanent tissues such as xylem, phloem and supporting tissues, while some stay meristematic so that growth goes on.
In plant Y, almost all the cells keep dividing, so they stay small and alike. Plant Y would be a soft mass of cells with nothing to hold it up or carry water.
